title: Karaoke bar customers danced as medics tried to save man, police say

evidence_packet.title: Karaoke bar customers danced as medics tried to save man, police say
evidence_packet.lead: Greater Manchester Police criticised management at a bar where a man was attacked
evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester Police criticised management at a bar where a man was attacked
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Karaoke bar customers danced as medics tried to save man, police say - BBC News Image caption, Shane Cullen died following an assault at Blues Cabaret and Karaoke Bar on Bow Street, Ashton-under-Lyne By George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporting Scheme Published 8 August 2026 Karaoke bar customers carried on dancing as paramedics fought to save a man's life, police have said. Shane Cullen, 31, died after being assaulted at Blues Cabaret and Karaoke Bar on Bow Street, Ashton-under-Lyne, on 11 July. Greater Manchester Police (GMP) told a Tameside Council licensing committee hearing that management did not shut off the music, stop alcohol sales, raise the lights or evacuate the premises "despite the severity of the situation". Tameside Council suspended the venue's licence for three months and ordered it to abide by conditions including increasing security staff before it can reopen. After the incident, GMP applied for a review of the bar's licence. In a statement served ahead of the council licensing committee meeting on Thursday, PC Craig Foley said the force had serious concerns, including about "significant failings in management, supervision, compliance and leadership". Image source, GMP Image caption, Shane Cullen's family say he was a "gentle giant" and would be "sadly missed" Foley said door supervisors outside had "no effective view" of events occurring inside. A bouncer was also noted to have witnessed a separate assault outside the bar "without intervening or acting". Foley said that officers attended the bar and helped clear a space for paramedics to begin commencing CPR. He wrote: "Despite the severity of the situation, alcohol sales continued, music continued to be played and customers continued dancing and congregating around the area where officers were admin

title: Manchester: Rapist who posed as 'good Samaritan' jailed

evidence_packet.lead: Mohammed Al Masri denied the offence and claimed sex was consensual but was found guilty at a trial in July

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester: Rapist who posed as 'good Samaritan' jailed - BBC News Image source, Greater Manchester Police Image caption, Mohammed Al Masri was jailed for eight years for rape By Haider Saleem BBC North West Published 8 August 2026 A "vile sex predator" who posed as a good Samaritan to an upset women after a Christmas drinks night out has been jailed. Mohammed Al Masri, 25, offered to get his victim a taxi home, but instead took her to his house where he carried out the sex attack, Minshull Street Crown Court heard. The woman said she thought she was "going to die" and was thinking about her children and "how they would be able to live without a mum". Al Masri denied the offence and claimed sex was consensual but was found guilty at a trial in July. He was sentenced to eight years for rape on Friday. The woman had been walking through Picadilly Gardens in Manchester, on 22 December, on her way home after a night out with a friend and was on the phone to her boyfriend. Al Masri, who speaks Arabic and has limited English, and another man followed her and approached her, pestering her with compliments before offering to get her home when she became upset. The pair offered to get her an Uber and she saw them type in her address and believed they were trying to help her, but inside the taxi she felt unsafe and shared her location with her boyfriend. The taxi driver later told police the woman had passed out in the taxi and the two men had helped her out the car. She was taken into the bedroom of Al Masri's house in Abbey Hey were Al Masri raped her, while his friend remained in the room. The woman's boyfriend had contacted police and shared her location. title: Meet Match of the Dames - the mission to get more women watching football

evidence_packet.title: Meet Match of the Dames - the mission to get more women watching football
evidence_packet.lead: Organisers say the game remains largely a "boys club" and want to get more women into the stands
evidence_packet.summary: Organisers say the game remains largely a "boys club" and want to get more women into the stands
evidence_packet.evidence_text: In the summer before Match of the Dames launched, founder Anne Morris walked around the stands at non-league Altrincham FC with one goal in mind - to count the number of women And the result - just a tiny fraction of the total crowd - gave her all the motivation she needed Morris told the BBC: "We think the stands have been a boy's club long enough "I walked around and the ground, the ticket gate was 1,200 and I counted about 88 women." A new project was born, and is now positively thriving In 2025, Match of the Dames , external first launched in partnership with Altrincham FC

title: Trains returning to normal after Manchester power disruption

evidence_packet.title: Trains returning to normal after Manchester power disruption
evidence_packet.lead: Rail services were returning to normal after an outage in Manchester on Thursday caused major disruption
evidence_packet.summary: Rail services were returning to normal after an outage in Manchester on Thursday caused major disruption
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The rail network across northern England has been returning to normal after a power cut led to major disruption for thousands of passengers While the power was only down for 90 seconds at about 13:40 BST on Thursday, the delay to back-up systems at Network Rail's Manchester Rail Operating Centre meant trains had to stop running Many services were cancelled and commuters faced "nightmare" diversions Network Rail said services had "largely been restored across the North West", but some disruption to TransPennine Express services remained while trains and crews returned to their usual positions Network Rail's route director for the North West, Chris Wright, said: "We're continuing to work closely with train operators to return services to normal as quickly as possible." Manchester Rail Operating Centre was opened in July 2014

title: How a 90-second power outage sparked chaos for train commuters

evidence_packet.title: How a 90-second power outage sparked chaos for train commuters
evidence_packet.lead: The incident raised questions about how a disrupted power supply can have such a widespread impact
evidence_packet.summary: The incident raised questions about how a disrupted power supply can have such a widespread impact
evidence_packet.evidence_text: But after commuters were left facing chaos , it has raised questions about how a short outage at one operating centre could have a widespread impact Network Rail will face scrutiny for how its systems coped and responded to the outage That's the publicly-owned body whose job it is to operate and maintain Britain's railway infrastructure. That means the tracks, signals, embankments and major stations It was at Network Rail's operating centre in Manchester that the problem started. Its operating centres are where crucial controls are housed that let trains run safely across the country, with Manchester's centre responsible for large parts of the North West It was hit by a power cut in the area, which was resolved within 90 seconds. Given the centre's importance, backups are in place. But questions have been raised about how they responded Chris Wright, north-west route director at Network Rail , told the BBC "we didn't experience a 90-second interruption," insisting its systems were back online sooner

title: Will there be Metrolink trams to Stockport and, if so, when?

evidence_packet.title: Will there be Metrolink trams to Stockport and, if so, when?
evidence_packet.lead: The new mayor of Greater Manchester is asked about long-awaited plans to extend tram services
evidence_packet.summary: The new mayor of Greater Manchester is asked about long-awaited plans to extend tram services
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig has said the plan to bring tram services to Stockport is "complicated" but moving ahead The much-called-for expansion of trams to the town was confirmed last summer when former chancellor Rachel Reeves made a commitment to pay for the project. It would see Metrolink trams extended from East Didsbury to Stockport Speaking to BBC Radio Manchester on Thursday, Craig said of the project, which is yet to progress: "It's moving, but it is complicated because you've got to work through the route and the costings." Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM), which owns the Metrolink system, said in November it was working with Stockport Council to make a business case Craig added: "What Andy gave his commitment to do was to begin the work to plan the route, to consult on that, and to figure out how much it was going to cost and where we would engineer it "That work is still ongoing and I've wanted to support that."

title: Acquitted husband did murder his wife, south Manchester coroner says

evidence_packet.title: Acquitted husband did murder his wife, south Manchester coroner says
evidence_packet.lead: Donald McPherson, who lived with wife Paula Leeson in Sale, had taken out £3.5m life insurance shortly before her death
evidence_packet.summary: Donald McPherson, who lived with wife Paula Leeson in Sale, had taken out £3.5m life insurance shortly before her death
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A convicted fraudster cleared in court of killing his heiress wife for her money did in fact murder her, a coroner concluded at an inquest into her death Donald McPherson, 53, was ordered to be found not guilty of murdering Paula Leeson, 47, on a judge's direction halfway through his trial at Manchester Crown Court in 2021 He had taken out £3.5m life insurance on the mother-of-one shortly before her 2017 death, the trial heard Manchester South Senior Coroner Alison Mutch told the inquest McPherson was in debt and the only person to benefit from the death, saying she was "therefore satisfied he did murder his wife" and recorded a conclusion of unlawful killing Two years ago Leeson's family, who run a successful plant hire business in south Manchester, blocked him inheriting his late wife's £4.4m estate McPherson has always denied any involvement in his wife's death, describing it a "tragic accident"

title: Karaoke bar customers danced as medics tried to save man, police say

evidence_packet.title: Karaoke bar customers danced as medics tried to save man, police say
evidence_packet.lead: Karaoke bar customers carried on dancing as paramedics fought to save a man's life, police have said Shane Cullen, 31, died after being assaulted at Blues Cabaret and Karaoke Bar on Bow Street, Ashton-under-Lyne, on 11 July Greater Manchester Police (GMP) told a Tameside Council
evidence_packet.summary: Karaoke bar customers carried on dancing as paramedics fought to save a man's life, police have said Shane Cullen, 31, died after being assaulted at Blues Cabaret and Karaoke Bar on Bow Street, Ashton-under-Lyne, on 11 July Greater Manchester Police (GMP) told a Tameside Council
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Karaoke bar customers carried on dancing as paramedics fought to save a man's life, police have said Shane Cullen, 31, died after being assaulted at Blues Cabaret and Karaoke Bar on Bow Street, Ashton-under-Lyne, on 11 July Greater Manchester Police (GMP) told a Tameside Council licensing committee hearing that management did not shut off the music, stop alcohol sales, raise the lights or evacuate the premises "despite the severity of the situation" Tameside Council suspended the venue's licence for three months and ordered it to abide by conditions including increasing security staff before it can reopen After the incident, GMP applied for a review of the bar's licence In a statement served ahead of the council licensing committee meeting on Thursday, PC Craig Foley said the force had serious concerns, including about "significant failings in management, supervision, compliance and leadership"

title: Meet Match of the Dames - the mission to get more women watching football

evidence_packet.title: Meet Match of the Dames - the mission to get more women watching football
evidence_packet.lead: In the summer before Match of the Dames launched, founder Anne Morris walked around the stands at non-league Altrincham FC with one goal in mind - to count the number of women And the result - just a tiny fraction of the total crowd - gave her all the motivation she needed Morris
evidence_packet.summary: In the summer before Match of the Dames launched, founder Anne Morris walked around the stands at non-league Altrincham FC with one goal in mind - to count the number of women And the result - just a tiny fraction of the total crowd - gave her all the motivation she needed Morris
evidence_packet.evidence_text: In the summer before Match of the Dames launched, founder Anne Morris walked around the stands at non-league Altrincham FC with one goal in mind - to count the number of women And the result - just a tiny fraction of the total crowd - gave her all the motivation she needed Morris told the BBC: "We think the stands have been a boy's club long enough "I walked around and the ground, the ticket gate was 1,200 and I counted about 88 women." A new project was born, and is now positively thriving In 2025, Match of the Dames , external first launched in partnership with Altrincham FC

title: Trains returning to normal after Manchester power disruption

evidence_packet.title: Trains returning to normal after Manchester power disruption
evidence_packet.lead: The rail network across northern England has been returning to normal after a power cut led to major disruption for thousands of passengers While the power was only down for 90 seconds at about 13:40 BST on Thursday, the delay to back-up systems at Network Rail's Manchester Rail
evidence_packet.summary: The rail network across northern England has been returning to normal after a power cut led to major disruption for thousands of passengers While the power was only down for 90 seconds at about 13:40 BST on Thursday, the delay to back-up systems at Network Rail's Manchester Rail
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The rail network across northern England has been returning to normal after a power cut led to major disruption for thousands of passengers While the power was only down for 90 seconds at about 13:40 BST on Thursday, the delay to back-up systems at Network Rail's Manchester Rail Operating Centre meant trains had to stop running Many services were cancelled and commuters faced "nightmare" diversions Network Rail said services had "largely been restored across the North West", but some disruption to TransPennine Express services remained while trains and crews returned to their usual positions Network Rail's route director for the North West, Chris Wright, said: "We're continuing to work closely with train operators to return services to normal as quickly as possible." Manchester Rail Operating Centre was opened in July 2014

title: How a 90-second power outage sparked chaos for train commuters

evidence_packet.title: How a 90-second power outage sparked chaos for train commuters
evidence_packet.lead: But after commuters were left facing chaos , it has raised questions about how a short outage at one operating centre could have a widespread impact Network Rail will face scrutiny for how its systems coped and responded to the outage That's the publicly-owned body whose job it i
evidence_packet.summary: But after commuters were left facing chaos , it has raised questions about how a short outage at one operating centre could have a widespread impact Network Rail will face scrutiny for how its systems coped and responded to the outage That's the publicly-owned body whose job it i
evidence_packet.evidence_text: But after commuters were left facing chaos , it has raised questions about how a short outage at one operating centre could have a widespread impact Network Rail will face scrutiny for how its systems coped and responded to the outage That's the publicly-owned body whose job it is to operate and maintain Britain's railway infrastructure. That means the tracks, signals, embankments and major stations It was at Network Rail's operating centre in Manchester that the problem started. Its operating centres are where crucial controls are housed that let trains run safely across the country, with Manchester's centre responsible for large parts of the North West It was hit by a power cut in the area, which was resolved within 90 seconds. Given the centre's importance, backups are in place. But questions have been raised about how they responded Chris Wright, north-west route director at Network Rail , told the BBC "we didn't experience a 90-second interruption," insisting its systems were back online sooner

title: Will there be Metrolink trams to Stockport and, if so, when?

evidence_packet.title: Will there be Metrolink trams to Stockport and, if so, when?
evidence_packet.lead: Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig has said the plan to bring tram services to Stockport is "complicated" but moving ahead The much-called-for expansion of trams to the town was confirmed last summer when former chancellor Rachel Reeves made a commitment to pay for the project.
evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig has said the plan to bring tram services to Stockport is "complicated" but moving ahead The much-called-for expansion of trams to the town was confirmed last summer when former chancellor Rachel Reeves made a commitment to pay for the project. I
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig has said the plan to bring tram services to Stockport is "complicated" but moving ahead The much-called-for expansion of trams to the town was confirmed last summer when former chancellor Rachel Reeves made a commitment to pay for the project. It would see Metrolink trams extended from East Didsbury to Stockport Speaking to BBC Radio Manchester on Thursday, Craig said of the project, which is yet to progress: "It's moving, but it is complicated because you've got to work through the route and the costings." Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM), which owns the Metrolink system, said in November it was working with Stockport Council to make a business case Craig added: "What Andy gave his commitment to do was to begin the work to plan the route, to consult on that, and to figure out how much it was going to cost and where we would engineer it "That work is still ongoing and I've wanted to support that."

evidence_packet.summary: A convicted fraudster cleared in court of killing his heiress wife for her money did in fact murder her, a coroner concluded at an inquest into her death Donald McPherson, 53, was ordered to be found not guilty of murdering Paula Leeson, 47, on a judge's direction halfway through
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A convicted fraudster cleared in court of killing his heiress wife for her money did in fact murder her, a coroner concluded at an inquest into her death Donald McPherson, 53, was ordered to be found not guilty of murdering Paula Leeson, 47, on a judge's direction halfway through his trial at Manchester Crown Court in 2021 He had taken out £3.5m life insurance on the mother-of-one shortly before her 2017 death, the trial heard Manchester South Senior Coroner Alison Mutch told the inquest McPherson was in debt and the only person to benefit from the death, saying she was "therefore satisfied he did murder his wife" and recorded a conclusion of unlawful killing Two years ago Leeson's family, who run a successful plant hire business in south Manchester, blocked him inheriting his late wife's £4.4m estate McPherson has always denied any involvement in his wife's death, describing it a "tragic accident"

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Andy Burnham The special wristband Prime Minister Andy Burnham wears everywhere - and what it means There's a touching story behind the eye-catching blue wristband. View 5 Images (Image: Jeff Overs/BBC/PA Wire) News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 07:46, 09 Aug 2026 Something unusual keeps showing up in all the many pictures of Andy Burnham - and it’s not just his now-famous eyelashes It’s a thin blue wristband that the new PM sports on his right arm, whether in BBC interviews, announcing key national policies, or meeting world leaders. And it has a very special meaning It’s linked to a little boy in Wigan who Burnham met a decade ago - and clearly never forgot That boy’s name is Joseph, and when he was born, his parents were told to take him home and enjoy the time they had left, because Joe wouldn’t live for very long View 5 Images Emma and Joe at the Wigan Athletics stadium

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Mottram Inside major bypass scheme on Greater Manchester border - 60 years in the making The idea to build a bypass in Mottram has been talked about since the 1960s, now its getting closer to reality View 6 Images M67 roundabout, pictured in July 2026 News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 07:27, 09 Aug 2026 Mottram was once a rural village with a smattering of farmsteads bordering Greater Manchester and Derbyshire Over the decades things have changed. Rolling fields and livestock have made way for houses, people and roads buzzing with cars The beautiful scenery can easily be admired by drivers passing by - because they’re usually stuck in queues in their cars. The A57 is a major route that connects Manchester to Sheffield, but it is notorious for having a huge traffic problem That problem is even worse at the moment as National Highways work on their solution - the Mottram bypass. This project, actually called the A57 Link Roads scheme, has been designed to reduce congestion and improve journey times and reliability across the Pennines Visible signs of the new bypass are already there. A maze of orange traffic cones surrounds the roundabout where the A57 meets the M67

evidence_packet.summary: Trains Broken down train in Greater Manchester causes more pain for railway passengers Delays are expected until 6pm tonight News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 16:25, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 16:25, 08 Aug 2026 View Image The line between Altrincham and Stockpo There's more disruption for
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Trains Broken down train in Greater Manchester causes more pain for railway passengers Delays are expected until 6pm tonight News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 16:25, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 16:25, 08 Aug 2026 View Image The line between Altrincham and Stockpo There's more disruption for railway passengers today after a broken down train blocked the line between Stockport and Altrincham Passengers are being warned trains could be cancelled or delayed by up to 30 minutes. The problems are expected to last until around 6pm Trains running between Chester, Mouldsworth, Delamere, Cuddington, Greenbank, Northwich, Lostock, Gralam, Plumley, Knutsford, Mobberley, Ashley, Hale , Altrincham, Navigation Road, Stockport and Manchester Piccadilly are affected In a statement National Rail Enquiries said: "A fault on a train between Altrincham and Stockport means that all lines are blocked. "As a result, trains running between these stations may be revised or delayed by up to 30 minutes." In a statement Northern said: "Train services are unable to run between Altrincham and Stockport in both directions. Services between Chester and Manchester Piccadilly will be affected by this disruption."

title: The huge plan for five new neighbourhoods in Manchester's student heartland of Fallowfield

evidence_packet.title: The huge plan for five new neighbourhoods in Manchester's student heartland of Fallowfield
evidence_packet.lead: Fallowfield The huge plan for five new neighbourhoods in Manchester's student heartland of Fallowfield University bosses hope that the accomodation site will be 'among the most sustainable in the world' View 4 Images A CGI of the Fallowfield developme News Andrew Bardsley Court r
evidence_packet.summary: Fallowfield The huge plan for five new neighbourhoods in Manchester's student heartland of Fallowfield University bosses hope that the accomodation site will be 'among the most sustainable in the world' View 4 Images A CGI of the Fallowfield developme News Andrew Bardsley Court r
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fallowfield The huge plan for five new neighbourhoods in Manchester's student heartland of Fallowfield University bosses hope that the accomodation site will be 'among the most sustainable in the world' View 4 Images A CGI of the Fallowfield developme News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 13:43, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 13:55, 08 Aug 2026 A huge £530m plan to create 3,300 rooms for university students in Fallowfield has reached a crucial next stage The University of Manchester has partnered with investors and a developer to create thousands of new, green residential spaces for students. The 24 acre campus, on land next to Wilmslow Road and Moseley Road, will be arranged into five neighbourhoods and more than 20 residential University bosses hope that the accommodation site will be among the most sustainable in the world'. The project has now reached 'financial close', with financial agreements signed off. Planning permission was granted last year It comes after the iconic Owens Tower accommodation block in Fallowfield was torn down last year, with former alumni who lived there including actor Benedict Cumberbatch, comedian Rik Mayall and Radiohead guitarist Ed O'Brien Work on the new development is expected to start next year, with the first rooms due to be opened in 2028

evidence_packet.title: Full list of 486 Wythenshawe roads where major change could be made
evidence_packet.lead: Wythenshawe Full list of 486 Wythenshawe roads where major change could be made A consultation runs until September 18 News Emily Parker Shopping Writer 10:21, 08 Aug 2026 View Image Netherwood Road, in Wythenshawe, where a 20mph speed limit could be Nearly 500 roads across Wythe
evidence_packet.summary: Wythenshawe Full list of 486 Wythenshawe roads where major change could be made A consultation runs until September 18 News Emily Parker Shopping Writer 10:21, 08 Aug 2026 View Image Netherwood Road, in Wythenshawe, where a 20mph speed limit could be Nearly 500 roads across Wythe
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wythenshawe Full list of 486 Wythenshawe roads where major change could be made A consultation runs until September 18 News Emily Parker Shopping Writer 10:21, 08 Aug 2026 View Image Netherwood Road, in Wythenshawe, where a 20mph speed limit could be Nearly 500 roads across Wythenshawe could see 30mph speed limits cut to 20mph. Manchester council is consulting on plans for the suburb in a bit to improve safety and 'create a more consistent road network' The changes on 486 roads would further align limits in the area with other parts of the city, with 68 per cent of roads already having 20mph restrictions, bosses said "Every year, around 1,000 people are killed or seriously injured on Greater Manchester's roads," the council posted on Facebook "Evidence shows that lower speeds can help reduce the severity of collisions and improve safety for everyone using our streets, whether you're walking, driving, cycling, or wheeling." The town hall said it doesn't expect the changes to have a 'noticeable impact on journey times', insisting research suggests delays across Manchester are caused by congestion at junctions, rather than the speeds of drivers

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Six people hurt in Bolton crash before car goes up in flames Police, firefighters and paramedics were called out to Moss Bank Way News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 10:00, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 10:46, 08 Aug 2026 View 2 Images The damage caused Six people were hospitalised following a crash which left one car ablaze and a casualty needing to be cut out of a vehicle Police, firefighters and paramedics were called out to Moss Bank Way in Bolton on Friday night (August 7). It followed a collision involving two cars. Greater Manchester Police said a man in his 30s has been arrested on suspicion of drink driving and remains in custody Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service said that a fire involving one of the cars had to be put out, and 'specialist equipment' had to be used to free a casualty. Police said the injuries sustained are not 'life-changing' A spokesperson for GMFRS said: “Shortly after 9:33pm yesterday evening (Friday 7 August), two fire engines from Bolton Central and Bolton North fire stations and an enhanced rescue unit from Leigh fire station were called to reports of a road traffic collision involving two cars "Crews arrived quickly at the scene. Firefighters used a hose reel to extinguish a fire involving one of the cars and specialist equipment to free one person

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts The Moonpig cards, love heart pendants and Amazon bracelets that exposed illicit relationships between prison officer pals and drug gang brothers Elle Walton's actions were discovered after her friend Jai Gascoyne's phone was interrogated View News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 09:14, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 11:12, 08 Aug 2026 The discovery of Valentine's cards, necklaces and bracelets exposed the actions of two 'corrupt' prison officers who had inappropriate relationships with two gangster brothers Jai Gascoyne, 25, and Elle Walton, 27, shared Valentine's cards with Dil Nawaz, 30, and Haq Nawaz, 32. The brothers were serving long sentences in HMP Buckley Hall in Rochdale after flooding the streets with up to £3m worth of class A drugs Gascoyne and Walton were both prison officers at the jail. Before locking them up yesterday, (August 7), a judge told the women that they had trust placed in them because of their jobs, and that they had 'undermined that trust in the most devastating way you could have' Manchester Crown Court heard that Gascoyne ordered matching necklaces and bracelets for her and Dil Nawaz. The female defendants also received money from associates of the brothers. Their relationships did not become sexual and they did not smuggle contraband on the Nawaz's behal Gascoyne admitted being in an inappropriate relationship with Dil Nawaz between January 20, 2024, and April 4, 2024. While Walton admitted being in an inappropriate relationship with Haq Nawaz between January 21, 2024, and March 16, 2024

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Dopey car thieves filmed themselves in Range Rover they'd just nicked Joel Wolfenden and Graham Cooke have been locked up News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 09:02, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 13:59, 08 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Graham Cooke, left, and Joe A couple of car thieves filmed themselves in a Range Rover they had just nicked. Joel Wolfenden and Graham Cooke, both 26, have been jailed for their part in a criminal operation that saw vehicles stolen from homes in Gorton and Levenshulme in January The pair were sentenced alongside alongside Kamran Khan, 36, who was filmed dancing inside a lock-up where stolen cars were kept. The trio were arrested following police raids in Wythenshawe, Stretford, Cheshire and West Yorkshire in March Greater Manchester Police said a chop shop was found in Frodsham. Vehicles stolen included a BMW X5, an Audi Quatro, a Renault Kadjur and a Mercedes Allied M8 Auto. A Skoda Kamiq engine, a Land Rover Range Rover gear box and a Mercedes E220D door trim were also found by cops The force said videos showed Wolfenden and Cooke driving cars they had just taken. It is thought there were at least 23 burglaries. Wolfenden and Cooke pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit burglary dwelling with intent to steal at properties between January 12 and February 3, 2 Wolfenden, of no fixed address, also admitted two counts of conspiracy to steal a motor vehicle, as did Cooke, of Harley Wood, Todmorden. Wolfenden was jailed for seven years and 10 months and Cooke for eight years and 11 months

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Andy Burnham The special wristband Prime Minister Andy Burnham wears everywhere - and what it means There's a touching story behind the eye-catching blue wristband. View 5 Images (Image: Jeff Overs/BBC/PA Wire) News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 07:46, 09 Aug 2026 Something unusual keeps showing up in all the many pictures of Andy Burnham - and it’s not just his now-famous eyelashes It’s a thin blue wristband that the new PM sports on his right arm, whether in BBC interviews, announcing key national policies, or meeting world leaders. And it has a very special meaning It’s linked to a little boy in Wigan who Burnham met a decade ago - and clearly never forgot That boy’s name is Joseph, and when he was born, his parents were told to take him home and enjoy the time they had left, because Joe wouldn’t live for very long View 5 Images Emma and Joe at the Wigan Athletics stadium

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Mottram Inside major bypass scheme on Greater Manchester border - 60 years in the making The idea to build a bypass in Mottram has been talked about since the 1960s, now its getting closer to reality View 6 Images M67 roundabout, pictured in July 2026 News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 07:27, 09 Aug 2026 Mottram was once a rural village with a smattering of farmsteads bordering Greater Manchester and Derbyshire Over the decades things have changed. Rolling fields and livestock have made way for houses, people and roads buzzing with cars The beautiful scenery can easily be admired by drivers passing by - because they’re usually stuck in queues in their cars. The A57 is a major route that connects Manchester to Sheffield, but it is notorious for having a huge traffic problem That problem is even worse at the moment as National Highways work on their solution - the Mottram bypass. This project, actually called the A57 Link Roads scheme, has been designed to reduce congestion and improve journey times and reliability across the Pennines Visible signs of the new bypass are already there. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan The 'couple's retreat' in Wigan attracting visitors from New Zealand After retrospective plans were passed the owner of the ‘shepherd’s hut’ holiday let said he was aware of 'the significant risks of refusal' Comments News Chris Gee Local democr Planning permission has been granted for a ‘shepherd’s hut’ and hot tub holiday let built on green belt land which has already been operating for more than a year Described as a ‘resounding success’ by its owners, the structure at Belle Vue, Lowton is described as ‘a luxurious, romantic countryside retreat’ designed for couples seeking ‘peace, comfort, and a deep connection with nature’ Originally built without planning permission, the owner of The Hut at Belle Vue said in its first 12 months of operation it had attracted 181 visitors, some from as far away as New Zealand Wigan council’s planning committee agreed with an officers’ report which said that although the plans had been submitted retrospectively, approval of the application was recommended Planners said that the impact on the green belt ‘is considered to be minimal when weighed against its limited footprint, modest scale, and discreet location within a well-established landscaped setting’

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Woodhead Pass Woodhead Pass has just reopened after a moor fire - now it's going to close again The road reopened on July 31 after being shut for more than a fortnight News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 17:44, 08 Aug 2026 View Image Woodhead Pass is to clo Woodhead Pass is to close for four more days this month for repairs on an historic drainage system The road - a major link between Greater Manchester and Sheffield - only reopened on July 31 after being closed for more than a fortnight due to the h uge moor fire near Tintwistle . Now it's going to be closed again for two days from Monday (August 14) and a further two days from National Highways say the closure is needed to allow a crane to carry out repairs to Woodhead Cascade, a series of stone steps that drains water under the road into Woodhead reservoir In a statement National Highways said the closures were originally due to take place on a weekend but 'various issues and concerns' meant the dates had to be changed. The statement added: "As part of ongoing work at A628 Woodhead Cascade repairs, which so far have been carried ou "Full closures are needed because of the size of the crane needed to facilitate the repair which will take up the whole carriageway. Diversions will be clearly signed. The scheme will continue until December 2026."

Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 17:04, 08 Aug 2026 A row building for years on a small Stockport allotment has now become a ‘war’ after a granddad was kicked off the site Rob McCurrie, 80, has had a plot at the allotment site on Newboult Road in Cheadle since 2018 but claims he has been forced off the site due to a ‘propaganda war’ waged by those in charge. The granddad said he has faced libellous accusations and has been the 'victim of accusation The allotment plot holder contacted the Manchester Evening News as he felt he had not been given a say and believes Stockport Council has ‘ignored everything’ about his side of the story A spokesperson for the National Allotment Society North West Branch said they would not comment as the matter has been dealt with and is now closed so no further action will be forthcoming. However the former construction worker said he was just ‘asking questions people do not li Mr McCurrie said: “I have been on the site for years. For seven to eight years, everyone was friendly. We got on and we all liked each other.”

evidence_packet.summary: Trains Broken down train in Greater Manchester causes more pain for railway passengers Delays are expected until 6pm tonight News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 16:25, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 16:25, 08 Aug 2026 View Image The line between Altrincham and Stockpo There's more disruption for
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Trains Broken down train in Greater Manchester causes more pain for railway passengers Delays are expected until 6pm tonight News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 16:25, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 16:25, 08 Aug 2026 View Image The line between Altrincham and Stockpo There's more disruption for railway passengers today after a broken down train blocked the line between Stockport and Altrincham Passengers are being warned trains could be cancelled or delayed by up to 30 minutes. The problems are expected to last until around 6pm Trains running between Chester, Mouldsworth, Delamere, Cuddington, Greenbank, Northwich, Lostock, Gralam, Plumley, Knutsford, Mobberley, Ashley, Hale , Altrincham, Navigation Road, Stockport and Manchester Piccadilly are affected In a statement National Rail Enquiries said: "A fault on a train between Altrincham and Stockport means that all lines are blocked. "As a result, trains running between these stations may be revised or delayed by up to 30 minutes." In a statement Northern said: "Train services are unable to run between Altrincham and Stockport in both directions. Services between Chester and Manchester Piccadilly will be affected by this disruption."

title: The huge plan for five new neighbourhoods in Manchester's student heartland of Fallowfield

evidence_packet.title: The huge plan for five new neighbourhoods in Manchester's student heartland of Fallowfield
evidence_packet.lead: Fallowfield The huge plan for five new neighbourhoods in Manchester's student heartland of Fallowfield University bosses hope that the accomodation site will be 'among the most sustainable in the world' View 4 Images A CGI of the Fallowfield developme News Andrew Bardsley Court r
evidence_packet.summary: Fallowfield The huge plan for five new neighbourhoods in Manchester's student heartland of Fallowfield University bosses hope that the accomodation site will be 'among the most sustainable in the world' View 4 Images A CGI of the Fallowfield developme News Andrew Bardsley Court r
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fallowfield The huge plan for five new neighbourhoods in Manchester's student heartland of Fallowfield University bosses hope that the accomodation site will be 'among the most sustainable in the world' View 4 Images A CGI of the Fallowfield developme News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 13:43, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 13:55, 08 Aug 2026 A huge £530m plan to create 3,300 rooms for university students in Fallowfield has reached a crucial next stage The University of Manchester has partnered with investors and a developer to create thousands of new, green residential spaces for students. The 24 acre campus, on land next to Wilmslow Road and Moseley Road, will be arranged into five neighbourhoods and more than 20 residential University bosses hope that the accommodation site will be among the most sustainable in the world'. The project has now reached 'financial close', with financial agreements signed off. Planning permission was granted last year It comes after the iconic Owens Tower accommodation block in Fallowfield was torn down last year, with former alumni who lived there including actor Benedict Cumberbatch, comedian Rik Mayall and Radiohead guitarist Ed O'Brien Work on the new development is expected to start next year, with the first rooms due to be opened in 2028

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wythenshawe Full list of 486 Wythenshawe roads where major change could be made A consultation runs until September 18 News Emily Parker Shopping Writer 10:21, 08 Aug 2026 View Image Netherwood Road, in Wythenshawe, where a 20mph speed limit could be Nearly 500 roads across Wythenshawe could see 30mph speed limits cut to 20mph. Manchester council is consulting on plans for the suburb in a bit to improve safety and 'create a more consistent road network' The changes on 486 roads would further align limits in the area with other parts of the city, with 68 per cent of roads already having 20mph restrictions, bosses said "Every year, around 1,000 people are killed or seriously injured on Greater Manchester's roads," the council posted on Facebook "Evidence shows that lower speeds can help reduce the severity of collisions and improve safety for everyone using our streets, whether you're walking, driving, cycling, or wheeling." The town hall said it doesn't expect the changes to have a 'noticeable impact on journey times', insisting research suggests delays across Manchester are caused by congestion at junctions, rather than the speeds of drivers

evidence_packet.lead: Bolton Six people hurt in Bolton crash before car goes up in flames Police, firefighters and paramedics were called out to Moss Bank Way News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 10:00, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 10:46, 08 Aug 2026 View 2 Images The damage caused Six people were hospitalised
evidence_packet.summary: Bolton Six people hurt in Bolton crash before car goes up in flames Police, firefighters and paramedics were called out to Moss Bank Way News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 10:00, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 10:46, 08 Aug 2026 View 2 Images The damage caused Six people were hospitalised
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Six people hurt in Bolton crash before car goes up in flames Police, firefighters and paramedics were called out to Moss Bank Way News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 10:00, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 10:46, 08 Aug 2026 View 2 Images The damage caused Six people were hospitalised following a crash which left one car ablaze and a casualty needing to be cut out of a vehicle Police, firefighters and paramedics were called out to Moss Bank Way in Bolton on Friday night (August 7). It followed a collision involving two cars. Greater Manchester Police said a man in his 30s has been arrested on suspicion of drink driving and remains in custody Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service said that a fire involving one of the cars had to be put out, and 'specialist equipment' had to be used to free a casualty. Police said the injuries sustained are not 'life-changing' A spokesperson for GMFRS said: “Shortly after 9:33pm yesterday evening (Friday 7 August), two fire engines from Bolton Central and Bolton North fire stations and an enhanced rescue unit from Leigh fire station were called to reports of a road traffic collision involving two cars "Crews arrived quickly at the scene. Firefighters used a hose reel to extinguish a fire involving one of the cars and specialist equipment to free one person

The female defendants also received money from associates of the brothers. Their relationships did not become sexual and they did not smuggle contraband on the Nawaz's behal Gascoyne admitted being in an inappropriate relationship with Dil Nawaz between January 20, 2024, and April 4, 2024. While Walton admitted being in an inappropriate relationship with Haq Nawaz between January 21, 2024, and March 16, 2024

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Dopey car thieves filmed themselves in Range Rover they'd just nicked Joel Wolfenden and Graham Cooke have been locked up News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 09:02, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 13:59, 08 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Graham Cooke, left, and Joe A couple of car thieves filmed themselves in a Range Rover they had just nicked. Joel Wolfenden and Graham Cooke, both 26, have been jailed for their part in a criminal operation that saw vehicles stolen from homes in Gorton and Levenshulme in January The pair were sentenced alongside alongside Kamran Khan, 36, who was filmed dancing inside a lock-up where stolen cars were kept. The trio were arrested following police raids in Wythenshawe, Stretford, Cheshire and West Yorkshire in March Greater Manchester Police said a chop shop was found in Frodsham. Vehicles stolen included a BMW X5, an Audi Quatro, a Renault Kadjur and a Mercedes Allied M8 Auto. A Skoda Kamiq engine, a Land Rover Range Rover gear box and a Mercedes E220D door trim were also found by cops The force said videos showed Wolfenden and Cooke driving cars they had just taken. It is thought there were at least 23 burglaries. Wolfenden and Cooke pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit burglary dwelling with intent to steal at properties between January 12 and February 3, 2 Wolfenden, of no fixed address, also admitted two counts of conspiracy to steal a motor vehicle, as did Cooke, of Harley Wood, Todmorden. Wolfenden was jailed for seven years and 10 months and Cooke for eight years and 11 months

evidence_packet.summary: Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 07:28, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 07:28, 08 Aug 2026 The UK's biggest solar eclipse in 27 years is fast approaching. On Wednesday (August 12), sky watchers across parts of Europe will be treated to an impressive celestial spectacle While tho
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 07:28, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 07:28, 08 Aug 2026 The UK's biggest solar eclipse in 27 years is fast approaching. On Wednesday (August 12), sky watchers across parts of Europe will be treated to an impressive celestial spectacle While those in parts of Spain, northern Portugal and Iceland are set to witness a total eclipse that will transform day into night. In the UK, however, only a partial eclipse will be visible - but there's something special about this one According to Royal Museums Greenwich, next week's partial solar eclipse will be the most coverage seen from the UK and Ireland since the 1999 eclipse A solar eclipse takes place when the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth, casting a shadow on Earth. Depending on where you are in the UK, up to 96 per cent of the Sun will be covered by the Moon The UK last witnessed a solar eclipse in March 2025, but only around 30-40 per cent of the Sun was covered by the Moon. Now, more than 90 per cent of the Sun will be obscured, causing the sky to dim as the Moon blocks our sunlight View 3 Images More than 90% of the Sun will be covered by the Moon in the UK (Image: AP)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Bolton council puts up 34 signs to help people find their way and encourage 'walking, cycling and wheeling' The circular signs are designed to 'make it easier for people to get around and find all the main attractions' News Chris Gee Local demo Bolton council has put up over 30 new signs around the town centre to help people find their way around and encourage walking, cycling and wheeling The 34 circular signs are in key locations like Victoria Square, Bradshawgate, Churchgate, Knowsley Street and outside the railway station They point the way to popular destinations like the Parish church, library and Queens Park, and tell people how long it should take to walk there The new signs also highlight the town hall, Bolton Market, Bolton Lads and Girls Club and the university and colleges Some signs feature motivational messages aimed at encouraging people to get around the town centre on foot, by bike or on scooters

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Andy Burnham The special wristband Prime Minister Andy Burnham wears everywhere - and what it means There's a touching story behind the eye-catching blue wristband. View 5 Images (Image: Jeff Overs/BBC/PA Wire) News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 07:46, 09 Aug 2026 Something unusual keeps showing up in all the many pictures of Andy Burnham - and it’s not just his now-famous eyelashes It’s a thin blue wristband that the new PM sports on his right arm, whether in BBC interviews, announcing key national policies, or meeting world leaders. And it has a very special meaning It’s linked to a little boy in Wigan who Burnham met a decade ago - and clearly never forgot That boy’s name is Joseph, and when he was born, his parents were told to take him home and enjoy the time they had left, because Joe wouldn’t live for very long View 5 Images Emma and Joe at the Wigan Athletics stadium

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Mottram Inside major bypass scheme on Greater Manchester border - 60 years in the making The idea to build a bypass in Mottram has been talked about since the 1960s, now its getting closer to reality View 6 Images M67 roundabout, pictured in July 2026 News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 07:27, 09 Aug 2026 Mottram was once a rural village with a smattering of farmsteads bordering Greater Manchester and Derbyshire Over the decades things have changed. Rolling fields and livestock have made way for houses, people and roads buzzing with cars The beautiful scenery can easily be admired by drivers passing by - because they’re usually stuck in queues in their cars. The A57 is a major route that connects Manchester to Sheffield, but it is notorious for having a huge traffic problem That problem is even worse at the moment as National Highways work on their solution - the Mottram bypass. This project, actually called the A57 Link Roads scheme, has been designed to reduce congestion and improve journey times and reliability across the Pennines Visible signs of the new bypass are already there. A maze of orange traffic cones surrounds the roundabout where the A57 meets the M67

Now it's going to be closed again for two days from Monday (August 14) and a further two days from National Highways say the closure is needed to allow a crane to carry out repairs to Woodhead Cascade, a series of stone steps that drains water under the road into Woodhead reservoir In a statement National Highways said the closures were originally due to take place on a weekend but 'various issues and concerns' meant the dates had to be changed. The problems are expected to last until around 6pm Trains running between Chester, Mouldsworth, Delamere, Cuddington, Greenbank, Northwich, Lostock, Gralam, Plumley, Knutsford, Mobberley, Ashley, Hale , Altrincham, Navigation Road, Stockport and Manchester Piccadilly are affected In a statement National Rail Enquiries said: "A fault on a train between Altrincham and Stockport means that all lines are blocked. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Dopey car thieves filmed themselves in Range Rover they'd just nicked Joel Wolfenden and Graham Cooke have been locked up News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 09:02, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 13:59, 08 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Graham Cooke, left, and Joe A couple of car thieves filmed themselves in a Range Rover they had just nicked. Joel Wolfenden and Graham Cooke, both 26, have been jailed for their part in a criminal operation that saw vehicles stolen from homes in Gorton and Levenshulme in January The pair were sentenced alongside alongside Kamran Khan, 36, who was filmed dancing inside a lock-up where stolen cars were kept. The trio were arrested following police raids in Wythenshawe, Stretford, Cheshire and West Yorkshire in March Greater Manchester Police said a chop shop was found in Frodsham. Vehicles stolen included a BMW X5, an Audi Quatro, a Renault Kadjur and a Mercedes Allied M8 Auto. A Skoda Kamiq engine, a Land Rover Range Rover gear box and a Mercedes E220D door trim were also found by cops The force said videos showed Wolfenden and Cooke driving cars they had just taken. It is thought there were at least 23 burglaries. Wolfenden and Cooke pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit burglary dwelling with intent to steal at properties between January 12 and February 3, 2 Wolfenden, of no fixed address, also admitted two counts of conspiracy to steal a motor vehicle, as did Cooke, of Harley Wood, Todmorden. Wolfenden was jailed for seven years and 10 months and Cooke for eight years and 11 months

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fallowfield The huge plan for five new neighbourhoods in Manchester's student heartland of Fallowfield University bosses hope that the accomodation site will be 'among the most sustainable in the world' View 4 Images A CGI of the Fallowfield developme News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 13:43, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 13:55, 08 Aug 2026 A huge £530m plan to create 3,300 rooms for university students in Fallowfield has reached a crucial next stage The University of Manchester has partnered with investors and a developer to create thousands of new, green residential spaces for students. The 24 acre campus, on land next to Wilmslow Road and Moseley Road, will be arranged into five neighbourhoods and more than 20 residential University bosses hope that the accommodation site will be among the most sustainable in the world'. The project has now reached 'financial close', with financial agreements signed off. Planning permission was granted last year It comes after the iconic Owens Tower accommodation block in Fallowfield was torn down last year, with former alumni who lived there including actor Benedict Cumberbatch, comedian Rik Mayall and Radiohead guitarist Ed O'Brien Work on the new development is expected to start next year, with the first rooms due to be opened in 2028

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts The Moonpig cards, love heart pendants and Amazon bracelets that exposed illicit relationships between prison officer pals and drug gang brothers Elle Walton's actions were discovered after her friend Jai Gascoyne's phone was interrogated View News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 09:14, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 11:12, 08 Aug 2026 The discovery of Valentine's cards, necklaces and bracelets exposed the actions of two 'corrupt' prison officers who had inappropriate relationships with two gangster brothers Jai Gascoyne, 25, and Elle Walton, 27, shared Valentine's cards with Dil Nawaz, 30, and Haq Nawaz, 32. The brothers were serving long sentences in HMP Buckley Hall in Rochdale after flooding the streets with up to £3m worth of class A drugs Gascoyne and Walton were both prison officers at the jail. Before locking them up yesterday, (August 7), a judge told the women that they had trust placed in them because of their jobs, and that they had 'undermined that trust in the most devastating way you could have' Manchester Crown Court heard that Gascoyne ordered matching necklaces and bracelets for her and Dil Nawaz. The female defendants also received money from associates of the brothers. Their relationships did not become sexual and they did not smuggle contraband on the Nawaz's behal Gascoyne admitted being in an inappropriate relationship with Dil Nawaz between January 20, 2024, and April 4, 2024. While Walton admitted being in an inappropriate relationship with Haq Nawaz between January 21, 2024, and March 16, 2024

evidence_packet.title: Six people hurt in Bolton crash before car goes up in flames
evidence_packet.lead: Bolton Six people hurt in Bolton crash before car goes up in flames Police, firefighters and paramedics were called out to Moss Bank Way News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 10:00, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 10:46, 08 Aug 2026 View 2 Images The damage caused Six people were hospitalised
evidence_packet.summary: Bolton Six people hurt in Bolton crash before car goes up in flames Police, firefighters and paramedics were called out to Moss Bank Way News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 10:00, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 10:46, 08 Aug 2026 View 2 Images The damage caused Six people were hospitalised
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Six people hurt in Bolton crash before car goes up in flames Police, firefighters and paramedics were called out to Moss Bank Way News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 10:00, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 10:46, 08 Aug 2026 View 2 Images The damage caused Six people were hospitalised following a crash which left one car ablaze and a casualty needing to be cut out of a vehicle Police, firefighters and paramedics were called out to Moss Bank Way in Bolton on Friday night (August 7). It followed a collision involving two cars. Greater Manchester Police said a man in his 30s has been arrested on suspicion of drink driving and remains in custody Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service said that a fire involving one of the cars had to be put out, and 'specialist equipment' had to be used to free a casualty. Police said the injuries sustained are not 'life-changing' A spokesperson for GMFRS said: “Shortly after 9:33pm yesterday evening (Friday 7 August), two fire engines from Bolton Central and Bolton North fire stations and an enhanced rescue unit from Leigh fire station were called to reports of a road traffic collision involving two cars "Crews arrived quickly at the scene. Firefighters used a hose reel to extinguish a fire involving one of the cars and specialist equipment to free one person

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wythenshawe Full list of 486 Wythenshawe roads where major change could be made A consultation runs until September 18 News Emily Parker Shopping Writer 10:21, 08 Aug 2026 View Image Netherwood Road, in Wythenshawe, where a 20mph speed limit could be Nearly 500 roads across Wythenshawe could see 30mph speed limits cut to 20mph. Manchester council is consulting on plans for the suburb in a bit to improve safety and 'create a more consistent road network' The changes on 486 roads would further align limits in the area with other parts of the city, with 68 per cent of roads already having 20mph restrictions, bosses said "Every year, around 1,000 people are killed or seriously injured on Greater Manchester's roads," the council posted on Facebook "Evidence shows that lower speeds can help reduce the severity of collisions and improve safety for everyone using our streets, whether you're walking, driving, cycling, or wheeling." The town hall said it doesn't expect the changes to have a 'noticeable impact on journey times', insisting research suggests delays across Manchester are caused by congestion at junctions, rather than the speeds of drivers

title: Why the 2026 solar eclipse will be the best in the UK in 27 years

evidence_packet.title: Why the 2026 solar eclipse will be the best in the UK in 27 years
evidence_packet.lead: Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 07:28, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 07:28, 08 Aug 2026 The UK's biggest solar eclipse in 27 years is fast approaching.
evidence_packet.summary: Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 07:28, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 07:28, 08 Aug 2026 The UK's biggest solar eclipse in 27 years is fast approaching. On Wednesday (August 12), sky watchers across parts of Europe will be treated to an impressive celestial spectacle While tho
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 07:28, 08 Aug 2026 Updated 07:28, 08 Aug 2026 The UK's biggest solar eclipse in 27 years is fast approaching. On Wednesday (August 12), sky watchers across parts of Europe will be treated to an impressive celestial spectacle While those in parts of Spain, northern Portugal and Iceland are set to witness a total eclipse that will transform day into night. In the UK, however, only a partial eclipse will be visible - but there's something special about this one According to Royal Museums Greenwich, next week's partial solar eclipse will be the most coverage seen from the UK and Ireland since the 1999 eclipse A solar eclipse takes place when the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth, casting a shadow on Earth. Depending on where you are in the UK, up to 96 per cent of the Sun will be covered by the Moon The UK last witnessed a solar eclipse in March 2025, but only around 30-40 per cent of the Sun was covered by the Moon. Now, more than 90 per cent of the Sun will be obscured, causing the sky to dim as the Moon blocks our sunlight View 3 Images More than 90% of the Sun will be covered by the Moon in the UK (Image: AP)

evidence_packet.summary: Bolton Bolton council puts up 34 signs to help people find their way and encourage 'walking, cycling and wheeling' The circular signs are designed to 'make it easier for people to get around and find all the main attractions' News Chris Gee Local demo Bolton council has put up ov
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Bolton council puts up 34 signs to help people find their way and encourage 'walking, cycling and wheeling' The circular signs are designed to 'make it easier for people to get around and find all the main attractions' News Chris Gee Local demo Bolton council has put up over 30 new signs around the town centre to help people find their way around and encourage walking, cycling and wheeling The 34 circular signs are in key locations like Victoria Square, Bradshawgate, Churchgate, Knowsley Street and outside the railway station They point the way to popular destinations like the Parish church, library and Queens Park, and tell people how long it should take to walk there The new signs also highlight the town hall, Bolton Market, Bolton Lads and Girls Club and the university and colleges Some signs feature motivational messages aimed at encouraging people to get around the town centre on foot, by bike or on scooters

Gascoyne ordered matching necklaces and bracelets for her and Dil Nawaz. The female defendants also received money from associates of the brother Their relationships did not become sexual and they did not smuggle contraband on their behalf. But the pair were both jailed as a judge warned a message should be sent out to female prison officers who may tempted to do the same Gascoyne admitted being in an inappropriate relationship with Dil Nawaz between January 20, 2024, and April 4, 2024. While Walton admitted being in an inappropriate relationship with Haq Nawaz between January 21, 2024, and March 16, 2024 Prosecuting, Philip Hall said that Buckley Hall is a category C jail with more than 450 prisoners, and about 200 staff. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts The New Year's Eve gathering that ended in murder Anthony Junior Murray murdered Joe Burton in Bury View 5 Images (Image: Kenny Brown | Manchester Evening News) News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 16:44, 07 Aug 2026 It should have been a night of celebration and socialising to bring in the New Year. But just minutes before the clock struck midnight last New Year’s Eve, a gathering in a first-floor flat in Bury became the scene of a horri It was there, in Anthony Junior Murray’s home, that he murdered his sister’s boyfriend Joe Burton. Joe was only 23 and had a young daughter. Their future together has been torn apart, and his family have been left bereft That night has created a lifelong feeling of grief and depression and of a gaping hole within the family. Addressing Murray, Joe’s mother Janette Keyworth said, in a statement read on her behalf in court: “Never in a million years did I think I would ever have to attend this tria “These are sights and words that no mum should ever have to endure, but I have those in my mind constantly.” Murray, 25, of Tarn Drive, Bury, was handed a life sentence for the murder of her son. He was told he would have to serve at least 18 years before he can be considered for parole. She said whatever sentence Murray received would ‘never be enough’

(Image: Christopher Furlong/Getty Im ‘The next stop is Piccadilly Gardens,’ says the neutral, automated voice as the bus pulls in. The new technology was one of the many upgrades buses were brought back under local control in Greater Manchester But, what if Manchester’s bus announcer had a Manchester accent? That’s the question one academic is asking as he tries to start a debate on the importance of local dialects “People might say there are more important things to worry about, but it’s a nice thing, and it gives people that extra opportunity to have a bit of pride in their community,” said Rob Drummond, professor of sociolinguistics at Manchester Metropolitan University. “The more people Professor Drummond’s call comes on the back of a research project he carried out called Westminster Voices, which focused on how speech can impact politics. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Friday 31 July 2026 at 11:11pm More than two million voters were eligible to vote in the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election as counting getsunderway. Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

title: "A devastating outcome": Trafford children's services rated 'inadequate' as Ofsted warns children left at risk of harm

evidence_packet.title: "A devastating outcome": Trafford children's services rated 'inadequate' as Ofsted warns children left at risk of harm
evidence_packet.lead: on WhatsApp Share via Email Trafford Council's children's services have been rated inadequate in two key areas by Ofsted, with inspectors warning that delays in responding to concerns about children have left some at risk of harm The report, published yesterday following a two-we
evidence_packet.summary: on WhatsApp Share via Email Trafford Council's children's services have been rated inadequate in two key areas by Ofsted, with inspectors warning that delays in responding to concerns about children have left some at risk of harm The report, published yesterday following a two-we
evidence_packet.evidence_text: on WhatsApp Share via Email Trafford Council's children's services have been rated inadequate in two key areas by Ofsted, with inspectors warning that delays in responding to concerns about children have left some at risk of harm The report, published yesterday following a two-week inspection between June 8th and 19th, judged both the impact of leaders on social work practice and the experiences of children who need help and protection to be inadequate - the watchdog's lowest grade Services for children in care were rated good, while support for care leavers requires improvement to be good Inspectors, led by His Majesty's Inspector Leanne Cooper, found that since the council's last full inspection in 2022 - when it was rated requires improvement across the board - leaders had failed to recognise and act on shortfalls in critical parts of the service The sharpest criticism was reserved for the council's "front door" - the point at which concerns about children are first reported. The report found that responses to contacts about children take too long, are not prioritised in line with risk, and that many children face lengthy Strategy discussions - urgent multi-agency meetings held when a child is identified as being at risk of significant harm - are too often delayed, leaving children in potentially unsafe situations for too long and at risk of what inspectors called unassessed significant harm

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Council's Community Safety Service was granted a three-year Criminal Behaviour Order (CBO) following repeated offences targeting retailers in Chadderton Athanial Lucas, 30, of no fixed address, appeared before Tameside Magistrates' Court on 29 July charged with three shoplifting offences at Londis in Chadderton Lucas was sentenced to eight weeks in custody, ordered to pay £513 in compensation and made subject to a Criminal Behaviour Order (CBO) until 29 July 2029 The three-year CBO was secured by Oldham Council's Community Safety Service, in partnership with Greater Manchester Police. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham has recorded participation rates above both regional and national averages while significantly reducing the number of young people who are not in education, employment or training (NEET) The latest Department for Education (DfE) Local Authority Participation and NEET figures for the 2025/26 academic year show that 93.2 per cent of Oldham's 16 and 17-year-olds are participating in education and training, an increase of 2.8 percentage points on the previous year. T At the same time, Oldham's combined NEET and Not Known (NK) rate has fallen to 4.6%, down 1.1 percentage points from 2024/25. This is significantly lower than both the North West average of 5.5% and the England average of 5.8% The figures also highlight Oldham's strong performance, in partnership with the charity Positive Steps, in tracking and supporting young people Positive Steps provides young people with support, careers advice and guidance after school, or between 19 and 25 if they have an Education Healthcare Plan (EHCP), helping them to move into education, training or employment Only 59 young people out of 7,177 are currently unaccounted for – 0.8 per cent of the borough's young people. This is well below the North West average of 1.3 per cent and the England average of 2.4 per cent

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A new exhibition coming to The Portico Library explores feminist themes of wellbeing, ageing and place in relation to magic and ritual healing Opening this October, Witches & Healers draws on Rosie Reed Hillman’s groundbreaking project Something That Was Ours , which explores what it means to be a witch today Hillman’s portraits of witches and healers are curated in dialogue with historic texts chosen by critical friends who identify with the practice of witchcraft and/or healing. The portraits, the books chosen, and their interpretation offer unique insights into the diverse lives an Using a mix of moving image and photography, the artwork builds a sensory and emotive portrait of women in midlife. Covering themes of menopause, mental health, climate change, and marital breakdown, this work explores the ways women have reclaimed the word witch and sought solac Speaking about the exhibition , Rosie Reed Hillman says: “I have worked to build rapport with contributors over the last four years and believe the intimate access conveyed in this project creates an exhibition that inspires empathy, curiosity and a greater understanding of issue “Women in midlife of all backgrounds are an overlooked demographic who want to see art and hear stories that reflect their experiences, and I hope this work speaks to them especially.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Central Library , Manchester Until 20 December 2026 Additional information Always double check opening hours with the venue before making a special visit Manchester has always been a city with stories to tell. This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City reporter in Seoul, South Korea Published 8 August 2026 Manchester City have agreed a deal to sign Argentina goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli from Marseille for £1.7m The 34-year-old returns to Etihad Stadium - where he spent the 2016-17 season without making a first-team appearance - and has signed a two-year deal Rulli famously scored a penalty in Villarreal's 2021 Europa League final victory over Manchester United, before denying opposite number David de Gea to decide the marathon shootout He has won eight caps for Argentina and was part of the squad that won the 2022 World Cup and 2024 Copa America Rulli has also had spells at clubs around Europe including Real Sociedad, Montpellier and Ajax He comes in as a replacement for England goalkeeper James Trafford, who left City to join Leeds in a deal worth up to £45m earlier this week, and will be understudy to number one Gianluigi Donnarumma
